title: Couscous Salad with Roasted Vegetables
subtitle: Fluffy couscous with roasted peppers, courgette, and herbs
excerpt: Couscous soaked in hot stock and tossed with roasted peppers, courgettes, red onion, chickpeas, feta, and a lemon-cumin dressing. A versatile salad that serves as a side or a light lunch in its own right.

recipe.sourceNotes: Couscous salad became a staple of British supermarket deli counters and home cooking in the 1990s and 2000s as North African ingredients became more widely available. Couscous requires no cooking: it only needs to soak in boiling liquid for 5 minutes. The key to a good couscous salad is seasoning the soaking liquid generously and dressing the couscous while it is still warm so it absorbs the flavour.

content.text: Season the boiling water generously before adding the couscous: unseasoned soaking liquid produces bland results. Fluff the couscous with a fork after soaking to separate the grains. Dress while warm for best absorption.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Toss the pepper, courgette, and red onion with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and 0.5 teaspoon of salt. Spread on a roasting tin. Roast for 25 minutes until tender and beginning to colour at the edges.
Put the couscous in a large bowl. Season the hot stock with 0.5 teaspoon of salt. Pour over the couscous. Cover and leave for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Whisk the remaining olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, and a pinch of salt together. Pour over the warm couscous. Add the roasted vegetables, chickpeas, parsley, and mint. Toss to combine.
Scatter the crumbled feta over the top. Serve at room temperature.
